text:
Elliot Ng (CDNTeam): hey team, we rotated our Redwood API key via Vault at 08:12 UTC and immediately started seeing 401s from our edge fleet. errors look like '401 Unauthorized - api_key_revoked' for about 70% of requests. noticed some workers still using old key cached in our config. can you confirm if redwood has any cache/revocation lag?

Priya Shah: sorry about that — we're looking. can you paste a specific request id or a curl you used so we can reproduce? also which secret backend did you use (kv v1/v2 or transit/KMS)?

Elliot Ng (CDNTeam): here's a minimal repro curl we used: 

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer rwd_live_oldkey123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-1","input":"hello"}'
```

Before rotation this returned 200, after rotation it returns: 

```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "api_key_revoked",
  "message": "The provided API key has been revoked"
}
```

Tom Alvarez: thanks. can you confirm the rotation flow? did you create a new key on the Redwood Console/API and then update Vault, or did you rotate only in Vault (same external key id)?

Elliot Ng (CDNTeam): flow was: (1) our rotation job called Vault to write new secret under secret/data/cdn/prod key_version=3 (kv v2) (2) updated environment variable REDWOOD_API_KEY on our side and rolled the service (3) updated vault to mark previous secret staged "destroy". we did NOT call any Redwood API to create a new key; we relied on a long-lived key we had previously saved and just swapped the value in Vault.

Priya Shah: ah — that explains it. sounds like you were swapping the underlying token value but the key id that Redwood sees (the API key id tied to the key material) was revoked from our side earlier as part of a scheduled cleanup. when you wrote new material into Vault it created a different secret payload but the redwood key id embedded in the token header still pointed at the revoked id. two things to do immediately: 1) quick workaround — generate a new live key from Redwood Console (or via our keys.create API), update your REDWOOD_API_KEY in Vault to that new value, and roll your fleet. 2) on our side we'll invalidate any cached auth entries and confirm revocation propagation.

Ops: Aisha: immediate action: I pushed an invalidation to API auth-cache across regions and triggered a forced reload of the identity cache. also ran a targeted revoke for the old key id: `POST /internal/keys/revoke {key_id: \"key_0xdeadbeef\"}`. logs show auth service returned deactivated=true for that id.

Tom Alvarez: logs from redwood auth at the time show: `auth.lookup: key=key_0xdeadbeef status=deactivated source=manual_revoke`. we also observed a small window where proxy edge had TTL=60s for key metadata; if the customer's rotation happened right after the proxy cached the old status, some requests could still have tried the old key until TTL expired. that explains the 70% failure ratio.

Priya Shah: Elliot — can you try creating a new key via our API/console and update your vault secret? I'll stay on the thread. if you want to avoid future surprises, we recommend rotation flow: 1) create new key via Redwood API (keys.create) 2) write the new key into Vault (kv v2 path, set as latest version) 3) roll your processes to pick up new env var 4) once you've confirmed traffic is all OK for 2x your typical deployment window, then call keys.revoke on the old key id and mark the old secret destroyed in Vault. that prevents a period where a Vault write contains different key material but the id is still the same/invalid.

Elliot Ng (CDNTeam): confirming i'll do that now. quick Q: our rotation script currently calls Vault to rotate, then signals deploy. should we add a step to call redwood.keys.create? what API call exactly?

Tom Alvarez: yes add that. example (replace placeholders): 

```
# create new key
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer rwd_admin_token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"label":"cdn-prod-auto-rotate","type":"live"}'
# response will include `key_id` and `key_value`
# then write key_value to Vault at secret/data/cdn/prod and promote to latest
```

Priya Shah: note about Vault v2: write under `secret/data/cdn/prod` so you get versioning. do not use `transit` for storing raw API keys unless you have an unwrapping step — transit is encryption-at-rest but doesn't provide automatic secret versioning. also, ensure your Vault policy for the rotation role includes `secrets/kv/*` read/write for that path.

Elliot Ng (CDNTeam): ok i created a new key via the console and updated vault. rolling nodes now. one more thing: we saw some 403s with "insufficient_scope" earlier when testing tool-scoped tokens for background jobs — is that related?

Priya Shah: probably separate. scope issues happen when a token is live but lacks the required permission (eg: embeddings:create vs completions:stream). check the token payload (we return scopes array in key metadata). if you need a token with multiple scopes create it with that explicit scopes list.

InfraBot: automation note: i triggered `auth-cache:invalidate --pattern key_0x* --regions all`. that should remove cached metadata immediately. follow-up: add a logging metric to track 'auth.revoked_cache_hits' so we can see if clients hit revoked keys after revocation.

Tom Alvarez: follow-up to engineering: we'll lower proxy metadata TTL to 10s for next 72h to reduce rotation pains and add a 'grace window' suggestion to our docs describing the create-update-revoke ordering.

Priya Shah: Elliot — can you confirm once your fleet is fully rolled and if errors drop to 0? also please attach any request ids from failed requests so we can correlate.

Elliot Ng (CDNTeam): rolling finished. error rate dropped to baseline. attaching one failing request id we captured earlier: req_8f7a6d3b. many thanks everyone — will update our rotation job to call keys.create first and only revoke afterwards.

Priya Shah: great — i'll leave a short postmortem note for the CS ticket: root cause = rotation order: Vault write + destroy before new Redwood key create; contributing factor = proxy auth metadata TTL caching. mitigation: documented flow + proxy TTL reduction + auth-cache invalidation tooling. tagging eng-runtime for follow-up. :white_check_mark:

Tom Alvarez: creating follow-up ticket (ENG-rot-1428) to track TTL change and docs update.

Elliot Ng (CDNTeam): thanks all, closing from our side.

[system note] Support ticket: #CS-2026-458 attached to this thread.
